name: Tom Barrett

data_centers.summary: Barrett moved to a protect-the-community stance in 2026. He wrote bills to keep data center siting decisions with local governments and to ban members of Congress from signing data center NDAs, and he cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act. Critics point out he voted for the 2025 tax law and the SPEED Act permitting bill and still campaigns on permitting reform, so the record is mixed but now leans toward guardrails.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett introduces Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act and No Data Center NDAs Act
evidence.quote: Families in my district are rightly concerned about the effect data centers could have on their utility bills, as well as the land and water in their neighborhood.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he frames data centers as a threat to bills, land and water and says residents should have the final say.

evidence.title: H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would bar federal agencies from overriding local zoning or using federal money to force communities to accept data centers.

evidence.title: H.R. 10118 No Data Center NDAs Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban members of Congress from signing secrecy deals about data center locations, water use or energy use.

evidence.title: H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on to the main bipartisan bill aimed at keeping data center power costs off household electric bills.

evidence.title: Campaign ad reported by The Cool Down via Yahoo: Barrett recasts himself as a data center critic
evidence.quote: I believe you should decide on data centers, not Washington.
evidence.what_it_shows: His general election ad runs on local control and a 2015 state House vote against a data center tax break.

evidence.title: The American Prospect: Barrett scrambles to bury his data center past
evidence.quote: Barrett also supported the SPEED Act, a permitting bill that passed the House mostly along party lines last December
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrary evidence: he voted for the 2025 tax law that extended breaks used by AI builders and for a permitting bill that would cut environmental review of data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett hosts energy roundtable on expanding production and lowering costs
evidence.quote: I've proudly led the charge to increase American energy production and strengthen competition in the market by advocating for permitting reform and rolling back burdensome regulations that have driven costs through the roof.
evidence.what_it_shows: He still pushes permitting reform and deregulation on energy, the build-faster side of the debate, even as he backs local control on siting.

ai_risk.summary: Barrett co-leads bipartisan bills to keep a human in control of any lethal AI weapon and to bar AI from making health insurance denials, and he cosponsored bills on chatbot age checks for kids and testing AI systems for nuclear-safety risks. This is targeted guardrails, not a broad AI safety regime.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett, Beyer, Jacobs introduce Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly critical role in strengthening our national defense, but it should never be the one making life-or-death decisions
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the Republican lead on a bill requiring human judgment before any AI-enabled weapon uses lethal force, and he offered a similar NDAA amendment.

evidence.title: H.R. 9729 Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Binding limit on military AI use of lethal force.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett helps introduce Doctors Not AI Act
evidence.quote: When it comes to someone's health and well-being, the outcome is too important to leave it up to an algorithm.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a licensed clinician, not AI, to make coverage denials, with disclosure of AI use to patients.

evidence.title: H.R. 10210 Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Targeted rule on AI in health insurance decisions.

evidence.title: H.R. 9965 AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs testing advanced AI systems and containing dangerous outputs, which his office describes as preventing risks to nuclear safety.

evidence.title: Press release listing his AI cosponsorships, including the CHAT Act on chatbots and minors
evidence.quote: require AI chatbots to implement age verification measures to protect minors
evidence.what_it_shows: His office says he cosponsored the CHAT Act requiring parental consent and suicide-risk alerts for minors using chatbots.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett leads VA Technology Modernization hearing on AI and claims processing
evidence.quote: must have necessary guardrails to ensure AI does not make decisions without human oversight or transparency
evidence.what_it_shows: As subcommittee chairman he pressed VA officials on human oversight and transparency for AI in veterans' claims.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett welcomes MSU engineering professor to discuss AI at VA subcommittee hearing
evidence.quote: keeping the paramount interest of veterans' consent and privacy and all of those things that we can't miss the mark on
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees benefits from AI at the VA but asks how to protect consent and privacy.

tech_regulation.summary: Barrett supports specific fixes such as age verification for AI chatbots and a ban on China-linked connected-car technology, but he voted against a committee amendment that would have limited police license plate cameras. The record is thin and leans toward targeted rules.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban sales of connected cars and car software tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Press release: Barrett says he cosponsored the Children Harmed by AI Technology (CHAT) Act
evidence.quote: require AI chatbots to implement age verification measures to protect minors
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a kids-online-safety style mandate on chatbot companies.

evidence.title: The American Prospect on Barrett's committee vote against limiting Flock license plate readers
evidence.quote: The amendment failed 44-20 in the House committee that Barrett sits on. Barrett voted no on the amendment.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrary evidence: he opposed a bipartisan Transportation Committee amendment restricting automated license plate readers to toll collection.

preemption.summary: Mixed and thin. Barrett voted for the May 2025 House version of H.R. 1 that carried a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, but in 2026 he introduced a bill barring federal agencies from overriding local data center zoning and campaigns against Washington deciding for communities. No statement found on the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: passage of H.R. 1 with the state and local AI-law moratorium (May 22, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Barrett voted Yea on the House bill that included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws; it was a vote on the whole package, not a stand-alone preemption vote.

evidence.title: Center for American Progress Action: almost every House Republican voted to block state and local governments on AI data centers
evidence.quote: arguing that Washington, D.C., politicians shouldn't dictate the future of data center development, despite voting to do exactly the opposite.
evidence.what_it_shows: Critics say his local-control message conflicts with his H.R. 1 vote for the moratorium.

evidence.title: H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Points the other way: his bill would stop federal agencies from overriding state and local siting authority for data centers.

evidence.title: The American Prospect quoting Barrett's virtual town hall remarks on 'nationalizing' data center decisions
evidence.quote: I said there have been these proposals to nationalize decisions that would override local communities about their decisions around data centers. And the people that I speak to overwhelmingly say that they don't want to do that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He now argues against federal decisions overriding local communities on data centers.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. Searches of his press releases and news coverage for Nvidia, export controls and chips turned up only a Michigan State chip-testing facility ribbon cutting and a ban on China-linked connected-car technology, neither of which is about export controls.

signature: Swing-seat Republican who pivoted in 2026 to data center local control and NDA bans and co-leads bipartisan AI guardrail bills on autonomous weapons and insurance denials.

notable_quote.text: Families in my district are rightly concerned about the effect data centers could have on their utility bills, as well as the land and water in their neighborhood.

groups: House Veterans' Affairs Committee, Subcommittee on Technology Modernization (Chairman)
search_notes: Ran about 12 Google News queries (data center, AI, chatbot/Big Tech, health insurance AI, autonomous weapons, Nvidia/export controls/preemption, CHAT Act/Section 230, town hall/SPEED Act) and pulled every barrett.house.gov press release URL across 15 listing pages via curl, then read the data center, autonomous weapons, Doctors Not AI, energy roundtable, VA AI hearing, chip testing facility, town hall and Speaker Johnson visit releases. Read the Prospect, Yahoo/Cool Down and CAP Action pieces and verified the H.R. 1 vote on GovTrack and his sponsorship of H.R. 10119 and 10118 and cosponsorship of H.R. 9340 on GovTrack. Not verified: the landscape lead that AnthroPAC gave $2,500 to Tom Barrett for Congress on June 29, 2026 (FEC API was rate-limited on every attempt, so it is not listed as evidence). GovTrack lists H.R. 7218 CHAT Act with zero cosponsors even though his release says he cosponsored it, so the CHAT Act item is cited as his statement rather than a cosponsorship. Detroit News (Aug 13, 18, 20) and WKAR pieces on his data center bill could not be opened because the Google News link decoder was rate-limited and the Wayback Machine was down; congress.gov returned 403. Neither Barrett nor McDonald Rivet appears among the 81 signers of the Nov 26, 2025 Matsui letter (PDF text checked).

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet

data_centers.summary: McDonald Rivet wants data centers to grow without raising household bills. She was an original cosponsor of the Energy Bills Relief Act, cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act, and signed a New Democrat letter asking for a national data center plan that weighs grid strain, water and consumer costs while calling data centers vital to the economy. No statement found on specific Michigan projects.

evidence.title: New Democrat Coalition letter to House appropriators requesting a National Strategic Data Center Plan (signed by McDonald Rivet)
evidence.quote: Rapidly increasing demand for data centers, driven by cloud computing and AI, is vital for America's economy and competitiveness. However, this expansion strains electricity grids, land, water, and community infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed on to a build-but-manage approach: data centers are valuable, but the federal government should plan for grid reliability, consumer costs and water use.

evidence.title: Press release: McDonald Rivet and New Democrat Coalition unveil Affordability Agenda
evidence.quote: protect consumers from bearing the costs of manufacturing and data center development
evidence.what_it_shows: As the coalition's freshman leadership representative she promoted an agenda that names data center costs as something to keep off consumers' energy bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs the main bipartisan bill to keep regular customers from paying for the power big new users like data centers need.

evidence.title: H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (original cosponsor, verified on GovTrack)
evidence.what_it_shows: Original cosponsor of the Casten bill making data centers pay their own grid costs.

ai_risk.summary: Her own Keep Call Centers in America Act would make companies tell customers when AI is handling the call and report AI-driven job losses, and she cosponsored the QUIET Act on AI robocalls along with AI research and education bills. These are targeted transparency rules; no statements found on frontier AI safety.

evidence.title: Press release: McDonald Rivet, Fitzpatrick introduce Keep Call Centers in America Act
evidence.quote: Require call center workers to tell customers where the call center is and/or whether artificial intelligence is being used.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bill adds an AI disclosure duty and a Labor Department report on job losses tied to AI, a targeted guardrail on AI in customer service.

evidence.title: H.R. 1027 QUIET Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires robocalls that use AI to imitate a person to say so up front.

evidence.title: H.R. 2152 AI PLAN Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Orders a government report on how criminals use AI for financial crimes.

evidence.title: H.R. 2385 CREATE AI Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a national public computing resource for AI research, a pro-research rather than restrictive stance.

evidence.title: H.R. 5351 NSF AI Education Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs AI scholarships and teacher training.

tech_regulation.summary: She backs targeted rules: AI robocall disclosure, forcing social media platforms to act on fentanyl sales, age checks to keep kids out of adult accounts, cutting off abusers' remote access to cars, and banning China-linked connected-car technology. She also belongs to the Monopoly Busters Caucus.

evidence.title: H.R. 1027 QUIET Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Higher fines for illegal robocalls and disclosure when AI voices are used.

evidence.title: H.R. 6259 No Fentanyl on Social Media Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes platforms report and crack down on drug sales.

evidence.title: H.R. 9706 Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushes online services to use age verification so kids cannot access adult products.

evidence.title: H.R. 2110 Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Car companies must cut off an abuser's remote access to a survivor's car data and apps.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Bans connected-car tech from China and other adversaries.

evidence.title: Press release: Keep Call Centers in America Act (her own bill on offshoring, automation and AI disclosure)
evidence.quote: Everyone knows the frustration of calling customer service and getting run through automated messages, when you need the help of a person
evidence.what_it_shows: She frames automation and offshoring as a consumer and worker harm that Congress should address.

preemption.summary: No public position found on federal preemption of state AI laws as of Sept 2026. She voted against H.R. 1 in May 2025 but her statement cited Medicaid, food aid and the deficit, not the AI moratorium, and she is not among the 81 signers of the Nov 2025 Matsui letter. No reaction found to the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: passage of H.R. 1 with the state and local AI-law moratorium (May 22, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted Nay on the package that carried the 10-year moratorium, but this was a vote on the whole tax and spending bill, not a stand-alone preemption position.

evidence.title: Press release: McDonald Rivet statement on voting against the tax package (H.R. 1)
evidence.quote: I voted no because gutting Medicaid, slashing food assistance, and adding trillions to the national debt will make things more expensive
evidence.what_it_shows: Her stated reasons for the Nay vote do not mention AI or state law preemption.

china_chips.summary: Leans hawkish but the record is thin. She cosponsored the Stop Stealing our Chips Act to pay and protect whistleblowers who report export-control violations, and she frames federal chip investment as making sure things are built in Michigan, not China. No statement found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales.

evidence.title: H.R. 6322 Stop Stealing our Chips Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Strengthens enforcement of chip export rules through whistleblower rewards and protections.

evidence.title: H.R. 802 STAR Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Extends the tax credit for building chip factories in the United States; about domestic production, not export controls.

evidence.title: Press release: McDonald Rivet, Peters, Slotkin announce $325 million CHIPS award for Hemlock Semiconductor
evidence.quote: In Congress, I will continue fighting to protect American jobs and make sure that we manufacture more here in Michigan, not China.
evidence.what_it_shows: She ties chip manufacturing to competition with China and supports federal money for domestic polysilicon and chip supply chains.

evidence.title: Press release: McDonald Rivet letter to USGS urging silicon and potash be listed as critical minerals
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames semiconductor inputs as a supply-chain security issue versus China.

signature: New Democrat freshman focused on affordability who backs keeping data center power costs off household bills and AI disclosure rules for call centers and robocalls.

notable_quote.text: Everyone knows the frustration of calling customer service and getting run through automated messages, when you need the help of a person

search_notes: Ran about 12 Google News queries (data center, artificial intelligence, electricity bills/ratepayers, chips/semiconductor/China, deepfake/chatbot/robocall/Big Tech, New Democrat/AI working group, Consumers Energy rate hikes, town hall data center, Whitmer/OpenAI/Oracle, call center/AI jobs, social media/privacy) plus a full-name AI query; none surfaced a direct data center or AI statement beyond her bills. Pulled every mcdonaldrivet.house.gov press release URL across 14 listing pages via curl and read the call center, China legislation, supply chains, Hemlock CHIPS, New Democrat Affordability Agenda, year-end report, identity theft and H.R. 1 vote statements; her committees and caucuses page confirms New Democrat Coalition leadership and Monopoly Busters Caucus. Downloaded and text-extracted the New Democrat data center letter PDF (she is a signer, dated March 19, 2026) and the Matsui preemption letter PDF (81 signers, she is not one). Verified her H.R. 1 Nay vote and her original cosponsorship of H.R. 7977 and cosponsorship of H.R. 9340 on GovTrack. Also read a Sept 3, 2026 Michigan Capitol Confidential piece in which she said market forces, not tax incentives, keep businesses alive after the SK Siltron wafer plant closed; it is about EV subsidies, not data centers, so it is not scored. Not found: any statement on the Saline Township or Bay City data center proposals, on preemption, or on Nvidia chip sales. NRCC ads attacking her over a China-linked battery plant (Gotion) are about state subsidies she backed as a state senator, not AI chips. Google News link decoding was rate-limited, congress.gov returned 403 and the Wayback Machine was down, so WCMU, MLive and ABC12 articles about her could not be opened; no AI super PAC activity for or against her was found.
